summary: Architecture/contract-clarification phase only (no production code modified; runtime unchanged, Observed/observe/unavailable). Independently re-derived Blocking Finding H-1's contractual cause from IWC-001 v1.2/IWPC-001 v1.3/PEC-001 v1.1/CHGR-001 v1.0 primary text, confirming Phase 145H's own conclusion: the root cause is a genuine implementation defect (FilesystemPendingReadinessStore.find_by_session_id never returning a consumed/ record), with a secondary, real contract-drafting gap in IWPC-001 v1.3's pending-scoped readiness-uniqueness language (IWPC-REQ-082/107). Classified the gap as a missing normative requirement and missing cross-contract uniqueness statement. Evaluated three alternatives (return the existing consumed package; reject with a new domain error; return a separate publication-completed result shape) and selected the first, confirming rather than merely deferring to the governing prompt's own stated preference: rejecting would narrow IWPC-REQ-024's existing unqualified idempotency guarantee (requiring a major version), and a separate result shape would duplicate a schema IWPC-REQ-023/054 already assign to readiness. Revised IWPC-001 additively to v1.4 (SS35): freezes the one-Human-Governance-Act uniqueness invariant (IWPC-REQ-197, keyed on the existing session_id, no new identifier introduced); extends the session_id-keyed idempotent-by-key readiness-construction guarantee across a package's entire lifecycle rather than only its pending state (IWPC-REQ-198/199, plus in-place, non-narrowing corrections to IWPC-REQ-024/082/107 mirroring the Phase 145C precedent exactly); states explicitly the upstream invariant PEC-001's package_id-scoped replay guard always implicitly relied on (IWPC-REQ-201); and adds explicit failed/partial-publication recovery semantics (IWPC-REQ-202/203, restating IWPC-REQ-089/154 unchanged), backward-compatibility and historical-inconsistency fail-closed rules (IWPC-REQ-204/205, reusing the existing persistence_corrupt error_type -- no new error or exit code introduced), and a normative readiness behavior matrix (IWPC-REQ-206). Independently confirmed, with documented reasoning for each rather than mere assertion, that IWC-001, PEC-001, and CHGR-001 each require no revision: IWC-001 already establishes at-most-one-Human-Governance-Act-per-session and has no jurisdiction over the Pending-Readiness Store (an IWPC-001-invented concept); PEC-001's package_id-scoped replay guard was always correctly scoped to what PEC-001 owns; CHGR-001 SS2's 'one Human Governance Act' language already states the definitional invariant one layer downstream of where the actual gap lived. No repair was performed -- H-1 remains open, pending a future, separately governed implementation phase (145H.2, recommended not authorized). See docs/PHASE_145H1_POST_CONSUMPTION_READINESS_UNIQUENESS_CONTRACT_CLARIFICATION.md.
